summary: Structure, file mapping, SILAC channel and genotype mapping, instruments and ontology terms hold up under independent checks. Two important findings remain. comment[sdrf version] names a specification version that does not exist (v1.2.0; the spec is v1.1.0). comment[cleavage agent details] records one enzyme per batch, but the Supplement says every pull-down was digested with LysC plus trypsin.

reviewer_context.context: fresh isolated subagent with no producer transcript; producer manifest and report treated as untrusted and re-checked against PRIDE, the Supplement, MaxQuant outputs, raw headers and OLS

spec_compliance.evidence: Columns, order, reserved words and NT/AC syntax are fine (sdrf-tools structure OK, no N/A or empty cells). But comment[sdrf version]=v1.2.0 on all 204 rows is wrong: the pinned spec README and upstream master README both say 'Version v1.1.0', and base.yaml's examples are v1.1.0. The repo holds 15k+ SDRFs with v1.1.0.

ontology_integrity.evidence: OLS4 labels resolved and none obsolete: BTO:0002181 HEK-293T cell, NCIT:C185409, MS:1000449/1000556/1001742, MS:1001309, MS:1001251, MS:1000133, PRIDE:0000325/0000326/0000627, UNIMOD:4/35/1/259/267, UBERON:0002113, NCBITaxon:9606, PATO:0000461/0000383. sdrf-tools check reported 15/15 verified with 0 UNIMOD swaps.

source_evidence.evidence: These match the Supplement, MaxQuant designs and Cellosaurus: HEK293T, DMEM, SILAC media, CID/DDA, 0.5 Da, modifications, and the Table S1 constructs. The cleavage agent does not: the Supplement ('Protein precipitation and in-solution digest') says LysC and trypsin were both used for all IP digests, but the SDRF records Trypsin only (rows 1-56) or Lys-C only (rows 57-204).

file_mapping.evidence: A fresh PRIDE files/all fetch (projectAccessions={PXD001942}) lists 122 .raw files. The SDRF references 102 unique ones, all deposited and all vendor raw. The 20 unannotated files are exactly the Tiffy_20120213 APP_48h whole-proteome slices, whose exclusion is documented. Each raw file has exactly one SILAC light row and one heavy row.

design_consistency.evidence: The channel convention '<A> vs <B>' = A light, B heavy is confirmed by the explicit ATXN1 mutL_vs_wtH file and by bait H/L ratios: EV-vs-bait gives H/L 23-72 and bait-vs-EV gives H/L 0.005-0.08 for PARK2, PSEN1, HTT, ATXN1 and APP. Genotypes match the experimentalDesignTemplate names for all five baits. No duplicate (source, assay, label) keys and no duplicate replicate coordinates. Biological replicates are consistent with Rep/date naming.

omission_safety.evidence: Instruments re-read from raw headers by HTTP range for 6 files across the Orbi6/Bert/Ernie/Tiffy batches, and all match the SDRF. Disease 'normal' is the cell line's, not PRIDE's project-level HD. Values marked 'not available' are honest. The HDex1 Q79-vs-Q145 conflict and the excluded proteome runs are disclosed in the manifest limitations. The cleavage agent issue is handled under source_evidence.

deterministic_validation.evidence: parse_sdrf validate-sdrf -t ms-proteomics -t human -t cell-lines -t clinical-metadata: 'Everything seems to be fine', exit 0. sdrf-tools check CLEAN, exit 0. sdrf-tools score 98/100, exit 0. sdrf-tools structure OK, exit 0. Logs are in the review-1 dir.

findings.message: v1.2.0 is the ms-proteomics template version (sdrf-pipelines bundle), not the SDRF-Proteomics specification version. Set it to v1.1.0.
findings.evidence: spec/sdrf-proteomics/README.adoc line 27 and upstream master README: 'Version v1.1.0'. base.yaml comment[sdrf version] is 'Version of the SDRF-Proteomics specification'. Repo distribution: v1.1.0 in more than 15,000 files.

findings.location: comment[cleavage agent details], rows 1-56 (Trypsin only) and rows 57-204 (Lys-C only)
findings.message: The digest used LysC plus trypsin for all pull-downs, but each row carries only one of them. Fix: annotate both NT=Lys-C;AC=MS:1001309 and NT=Trypsin;AC=MS:1001251 on every row using two comment[cleavage agent details] columns, or cite batch-specific evidence of a different digest. The producer's statement that 'only one cleavage agent column is licensed' is contradicted by repo practice.
findings.evidence: Supplement mmc1, 'Protein precipitation and in-solution digest': 'Lysyl endopeptidase (LysC) ... and sequence-grade modified Trypsin ... was used for in-solution digestion.' The Mascot 'LysC specificity' is a search setting, not the digest. 1,759 SDRFs in sdrf-annotated-datasets carry repeated cleavage agent columns, and parse_sdrf accepts them. As written, a reprocessing search on rows 57-204 would drop arginine-terminated peptides.

findings.message: ms-proteomics 1.2.0 exists only in the installed sdrf-pipelines bundle (its new QC fields are marked experimental). The pinned spec submodule and upstream templates.yaml list latest 1.1.0. Consider v1.1.0.
findings.evidence: spec templates.yaml: ms-proteomics latest 1.1.0. 554 repo files nevertheless use VV=v1.2.0.

findings.message: The excluded whole-proteome runs are documented. They could be annotated later if the APP/APPsw channel map is recovered, for example from the authors.
findings.evidence: The proteome_changes_APPsw design gives only Exp3/Exp4 with no construct-to-channel map.

findings.message: Arg-10 is justified by the heavy medium, but the original 1.0.13.13 searches quantified Lys-8 only. This is disclosed in the limitations and needs no change.

Optional improvements: add characteristics[genetic modification]=overexpression (clinical-metadata licenses it) to describe the transient myc-bait transfection, and add characteristics[developmental stage] from Cellosaurus 'Fetus'. comment[precursor mass tolerance] is absent because no source records it.
findings.evidence: clinical-metadata.yaml genetic modification examples include 'overexpression'. sdrf-tools score lists developmental stage and precursor tolerance as missing recommended columns.
